newsitem.title: CUBA: Peru's Fujimori due to arrive in Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori due to arrive in Cuba.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori was due to arrive in Havana on Monday on a previously unannounced trip to Cuba, a Peruvian Embassy official said.
Embassy official Cesar Larrain told reporters at Havana's Jose Marti airport that Fujimori would be flying in after visiting the Dominican Republic.

Larrain did not give details but the Peruvian leader was believed to be seeking to discuss ways of resolving the 76-day-old Lima hostage crisis, in which Marxist rebels are holding 72 men hostage at the Japanese ambassador's residence.

Tight security at Havana airport suggested that President Fidel Castro could meet Fujimori on his arrival. Cuban government officials had earlier asked some foreign reporters to go to the airport to cover an arrival there, but they did not confirm that Fujimori was coming.

News reports have said Cuba, Nicaragua or a country in Eastern Europe could be potential places of asylum for the hostage-takers. However, the Cuban government has consistently declined to make any comment on such speculation. Fujimori has said he has not spoken to Castro about asylum for the rebels.

While ruling out considering the main demand of the rebels - - release of 400 jailed comrades -- Fujimori has indicated he might make other concessions. He has always left the way open to asylum in another country for the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary (MRTA) rebels, who seized their captives Dec 17.
